S7.01.note: Centring is CSS (.empty-state uses justify-content: center in a flex transcript); the code does not measure it, so check by eye.
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the Activity Bar to open the sidebar.
If the transcript already has messages, click the New chat (+) button in the header.
Look at the empty transcript area: the headline 'Start a conversation' and the line 'Ask about your code or describe a change.' should sit in the middle of the area, above the composer.
Resize the window and check the start view stays centred.
S7.01.where: AGI Code (sidebar) > New chat (+) button in the header

S7.02.needs: a conversation with at least one reply
S7.02.note: The width comes from the --conversation-width value of 768px in webviewContent.ts; the column is set by CSS padding on the transcript.
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the Activity Bar.
Click the Sessions button (clock icon, hover title 'Sessions') in the header.
Click a conversation that already has replies.
Widen the VS Code window a lot, then narrow it.
Look that the message text stays in one centred column of about 768 px, with empty space on both sides when wide.
S7.02.where: AGI Code (sidebar) > Sessions (clock icon in the header) > open a conversation that has replies

S7.04.needs: a conversation that has produced an artifact
S7.04.note: The artifact is opened with showTextDocument in the active editor group and no column is given, so it may open in the chat's group rather than beside it; the code does not force a split.
steps: Open a conversation that has produced an artifact (AGI Code sidebar or Code: Open Chat in Editor).
Press Cmd+Shift+P, type 'Code: Show Artifacts' and press Enter.
Choose an artifact from the list under 'Open an artifact…'.
Look whether the artifact opens in its own tab beside the conversation, with both visible and usable at once.
S7.04.where: Command Palette > Code: Show Artifacts > choose an artifact under 'Open an artifact…'

S7.07.needs: a project folder open in VS Code, optionally a git repository with changes
S7.07.note: The side-by-side layout is VS Code's own sidebar and editor layout; the extension only registers the sidebar and opens chat tabs.
steps: Open a project folder in VS Code and open a file in the editor.
Click the AGI Code icon in the Activity Bar so the chat shows beside the editor.
Optionally press Cmd+Shift+P, type 'Code: Git Diff' and press Enter to show changes.
Look that the conversation, the editor and any diff are visible together in one window.
S7.07.where: AGI Code (sidebar) beside the editor, or Command Palette > Code: Open Chat in Editor, with Code: Git Diff for changes

S7.08.needs: a signed-in account to send messages
S7.08.note: The side-by-side split is done by VS Code's drag, not by extension code; each chat is a separate panel.
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type 'Code: Open Chat in Editor' and press Enter.
Repeat step 1 so a second chat tab opens (the second is titled 'AGI Chat 2').
Drag one chat tab to the right edge of the editor area so both sit side by side.
Send a short message in each chat and look that both stay visible and usable.
S7.08.where: Command Palette > Code: Open Chat in Editor (run twice), then drag one 'AGI Chat' tab to the side of the other

S7.09.needs: a signed-in account to send messages
S7.09.note: Stacking is VS Code's editor-group drag behaviour; no extension code builds a stacked layout.
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type 'Code: Open Chat in Editor' and press Enter.
Repeat step 1 to open a second chat tab.
Drag one chat tab to the bottom edge of the editor area so it sits below the other.
Send a short message in each chat and look that both stay visible and usable.
S7.09.where: Command Palette > Code: Open Chat in Editor (run twice), then drag one 'AGI Chat' tab to the bottom edge of the editor area

S7.12.note: The usage banner also collapses with a button titled 'Collapse meter' and reopens from 'Show usage details'; the Sessions control is the secondary navigation.
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the Activity Bar.
Click the Sessions button in the header (clock icon, hover title 'Sessions').
Click the Close button (hover title 'Close') at the top of the Sessions panel.
Look that the Sessions panel hides and the transcript comes back.
Click Sessions again and look that it reopens.
S7.12.where: AGI Code (sidebar) > Sessions (clock icon in the header) > Close

S7.13.note: The extension declares the view only in the Activity Bar container; moving and remembering the spot is VS Code's own behaviour, and the extension does not pin it.
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the Activity Bar.
Drag the AGI Code view to the right edge of the window (Secondary Side Bar) or to the bottom panel area.
Look that the view now sits in the new edge.
Quit and reopen VS Code and look whether the view is still in the new place.
S7.13.where: AGI Code in the Activity Bar > drag the AGI Code panel to the right side bar or the bottom panel

S7.14.needs: a signed-in account to send messages
S7.14.note: The detach uses VS Code's built-in tab menu, whose item wording is not in this repository, so the exact menu text is unverified.
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type 'Code: Open Chat in Editor' and press Enter.
Right-click the 'AGI Chat' tab.
Choose VS Code's option that moves the editor into a new window.
Look that the chat opens in its own OS window and can still send a message.
S7.14.where: Command Palette > Code: Open Chat in Editor, then right-click the 'AGI Chat' tab and move it to a new window using VS Code's tab menu

S7.15.note: Searched apps/extension-vscode for 'Full screen', 'Fullscreen', 'Maximi' and 'Expand' in package.json and src; no extension command or control for a full-screen editor was found, only VS Code's own window or Zen Mode.

S7.20.needs: a conversation with enough messages to scroll
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the Activity Bar.
Open or make a conversation with enough messages to scroll.
Scroll the transcript up with the mouse wheel or trackpad.
Look that the 'Describe a task…' box stays anchored at the bottom while the messages scroll above it.
S7.20.where: AGI Code (sidebar) > the 'Describe a task…' box at the bottom

S7.21.note: The code caps the box at 140 px (Math.min(scrollHeight, 140)), so it does not open a separate larger editor.
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the Activity Bar.
Click into the 'Describe a task…' box.
Type or paste a long prompt of several lines.
Look that the box grows taller as lines are added, up to about 140 px, then scrolls inside itself.
S7.21.where: AGI Code (sidebar) > the 'Describe a task…' box at the bottom

steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the Activity Bar.
Click Sessions in the header (clock icon) and open a long conversation, then close Sessions with Close.
Scroll the transcript with the mouse wheel.
Look that only the transcript moves, while the header and the 'Describe a task…' box stay in place.
Scroll over the header or composer and look that the transcript does not move.
S7.22.where: AGI Code (sidebar) > open a conversation with many messages > scroll the transcript

S7.30.needs: a signed-in account that shows the usage banner
S7.30.note: The code saves only the usage-meter collapse (workspace state) and restores open chat tabs through a serializer; it does not save panel widths, which VS Code controls.
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the Activity Bar and find the usage banner.
Click its × button (hover title 'Collapse meter'); look that it shrinks to a 'Usage' pill.
Quit and reopen VS Code in the same folder, or run Developer: Reload Window from the Command Palette.
Look that the usage banner is still collapsed to the 'Usage' pill.
Optionally run Code: Open Chat in Editor, reload, and look whether the AGI Chat tab comes back.
S7.30.where: AGI Code (sidebar) > the usage banner's 'Collapse meter' button (×), then reload VS Code
